## 2. WHAT THE DRIFT LOOKS LIKE FROM THE INSIDE, AND THAT NOBODY CAME BACK TO ARGUE A STATE

**THE ENGINE OF BATCH 0004 AND ITS FINDING, STATED ONCE. A STATE GIVEN ON A DAY IS A STATE ABOUT THE PERSON WHO GAVE IT. There is nobody in this city who can require a records supervisor to say what a thing is, so the only thing anybody can be handed is what a man saw from where he was standing at ten past ten on a Tuesday, and that is a true sentence, and it is in a hand, and it has a date on it, and it is wrong.**

**THE FIRST VISIBLE ARTEFACT OF THE DRIFT, STAGED IN CHAPTER 0131, MONDAY 16 MARCH 2015, AND IT COST NOBODY ANYTHING.** A man of about sixty, a carter with a galvanised can he puts nothing into and has never been in that vestibule in his life, asked what was in the trough by the lock-ups ON THE SECOND OF FEBRUARY. **She answered him in about eleven seconds, in three halves, and gave the state, and the state was right about the second of February and wrong about the trough, and the wrongness is not a fault of the counter. It is a fact about a Tuesday. The man standing in front of her had a bowser to fill and a lunchtime to decide by and told her what he could see from where he was standing, and she wrote it down because he asked her what was true on a day, and she is not required to make a state and nobody can make her. The green in the bottom of that trough was what a market has been putting in a trough for forty years, settling out of water that came off a roof, and what the man put in himself was not what made it green, and that was not said to him as a fact, because a records counter with an opinion about a trough is a service. He went out with the can and did not put the drum in. Nobody was hurt. Nobody was helped. The register did not move.**

**AND THE SECOND KIND OF DRIFT, WHICH IS WORSE, AND IT IS JONAS'S FINDING OF CHAPTER 0131, IN FOUR LINES IN A PAD IN A SHOP: a state that has gone stale belongs to a THING, and a thing is out there and anybody may look at it, and that is the closest this borough gets to a correction and it has no form in it. A state that has been contradicted belongs to a PERSON, and it cannot be looked at, because the only person who can contradict it is the man who said it, and he has not come back, and nobody can ask him to, and a person may not be required to answer anything including a correction. ONE HAS AN OWNER AND THE OTHER HAS A PERSON, AND THIS BOROUGH HAS NO INSTRUMENT FOR EITHER. The first kind rots. The second kind cannot be moved at all, and the second kind is the one in the drawer under that counter.**

**AND NOBODY CAME BACK TO ARGUE A STATE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF IT. ABU BAKAYOKO'S FIRST SLIP, FIVE NODES ON ONE SLIP, DATED 26 JANUARY 2015, IS SEVEN WEEKS OLD AND IS IN AN INSIDE POCKET AND HAS NOT BEEN LOOKED AT SINCE THE DAY HE WROTE IT DOWN IN FRONT OF HER. He came on 2 February and on 13 February and has not come since, and it is a Friday, and if he comes on a Friday for another four years that is not a man, that is a rota with one name on it that nobody wrote down and that nobody could write down. HE IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO COULD CORRECT ANYTHING HE WAS TOLD AND HE IS NOT COMING BACK AND THERE IS NO REASON HE WOULD.**

**AND CHAPTER 0138 IS THE INSIDE OF IT, AND IT IS THE FINDING OF THE MONTH. A STATE GIVEN ON A DAY STOPS BEING A STATE ABOUT A DAY AND BECOMES AN OBJECT IN A COAT. It then needs a procedure, and there is no procedure on the sheet, because there is no name box and no number and no box at all, and a document with no procedure cannot be paid, cannot be returned, cannot be filed and cannot be destroyed. So it goes in a pocket. And nobody comes back to argue it, because a man with a piece of paper in a coat has no way of knowing whether he has been told something true, and the only way to know is to go back and ask, and going back is a decision, and nobody is required to make a decision. **That is the drift, and it is not a thing the counter does. It is a thing that happens to a person who is handed a correct answer and given nothing to do with it.**

## 3. THE SHELF, AND WHY NINE AND ELEVEN MAY NEVER BE ADDED

**NINE PIECES OF PAPER WERE IN THE DRAWER UNDER THE GROUND-FLOOR COUNTER AS AT 9 MARCH 2015 AND THERE ARE MORE NOW AND NOBODY CAN SAY HOW MANY, WHICH IS CORRECT. IN CHAPTER 0138 JONAS MERCER WROTE THAT THE NUMBER IS NOT NINE ANY MORE AND THAT HE HAS NOT COUNTED IT AND IS NOT GOING TO AND SHE IS NOT GOING TO TELL HIM. NOBODY, INCLUDING THE NARRATION AND INCLUDING JONAS MERCER, STATES A COUNT OF THE DRAWER AFTER 9 MARCH 2015, AND IN CHAPTER 0136 SHE IS ASKED FOR A DAY AND REFUSES WITHOUT A FIGURE, AND IN CHAPTER 0131 SHE DECLINES TO ASK FOR A DAY WITHOUT ONE, AND IN NEITHER CASE DOES ANYBODY PUT A NUMBER IN HER MOUTH. THIS IS THE BATCH'S HARDEST RULE AND IT HOLDS.**

**THE NINE, EXACTLY, AS AT 9 MARCH 2015, UNCHANGED: 26 January, Abu Bakayoko, five nodes on one slip · 2 February, Abu, the trough · 2 February, Emmanuel Otieno, the tap on the yard wall · 4 February, Otieno · 5 February, Howard Bramble, the standpipe at the bottom of his car park · 5 February, Otieno · 6 February, Otieno · 13 February, Abu, five things with the sixth declined · and one written on a Friday afternoon in the last week of February to somebody who was not in a room with anybody, about whom nobody has said a word and nobody is going to.**

**A TENTH SLIP WAS WRITTEN ON MONDAY 16 MARCH 2015 AND IT IS ABOUT THE TROUGH BY THE LOCK-UPS, it went into the inside of a coat, and on 20 April the man who is carrying it asked whether it was a receipt, and it is not a receipt, and it cannot be paid, cannot be returned, cannot be filed and cannot be thrown away, and he put it back in the inside of his coat, where it had been, and that was the end of it, and nobody helped him and nobody was harmed. HE IS NOT ON ANY LIST.**

**NINA Calder gives no count to anybody. Nobody in this batch asked her for one and Jonas Mercer did not ask her and did not count the drawer and did not look. THE NUMBER IS THE COUNT OF THIS ACCOUNT AND NOT THE COUNT OF A PERSON AND NO CHARACTER KNOWS IT.**

**NINE SLIPS IS A COUNT OF DOCUMENTS. ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE A DAY IS A COUNT OF PEOPLE. THEY ARE TWO NUMBERS ABOUT TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THEY MAY NEVER BE ADDED TOGETHER, and there is still no form in this borough, on any counter, on any tray, in any office, on which anybody could write that they are not a series, and a box that says *not a series* is a series. The reason is hers and was given out loud on 2 February: a slip is only written when a person stands in front of her and asks what was true on a day, and a form that added the two together would be a form that said *this counter sees eleven people and produces one document*, and that is a level of service, and there is no level of service in that room. THE THROUGHPUT IS ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE A DAY AND WENT UP FROM ABOUT NINE ON THE TWENTY-SIXTH OF JANUARY, AND IT IS ON THE BACK OF A HAND AND IN NO BOOK. IN CHAPTER 0132 HE COUNTED THE PEOPLE THROUGH THE DOOR ONCE, BETWEEN ABOUT TEN PAST THREE AND ABOUT HALF PAST THREE, AND HE COUNTED FIVE, WHICH IS NOT A DAILY FIGURE, AND HE STOPPED, AND THE REASON HE STOPPED IS A FINDING AND NOT A VICTORY: a count of people through a door is a level of service the moment anybody can be held to it, and the day a man can be held to it there is a morning somebody can say *we can only do eight today* and be entirely correct, and he came within about nine seconds of being the man who started.**

**AND THE THING THE PEOPLE WHO COME IN ARE NOT: SOMEBODY WHO ASKS A QUESTION ABOUT A DAY HAS ALREADY DECIDED THAT A DATE IS WORTH HAVING, AND THAT DECISION TAKES SOMEBODY ABOUT FOUR MONTHS AND A TROUGH, AND IT IS NOT SOMETHING A COUNTER CAN HAND OUT, AND IF THE COUNTER HANDED IT OUT IT WOULD BE A SERVICE AND IT WOULD SCALE AND IT WOULD BE A THING YOU COULD BUY. SOMEBODY WHO DOES NOT ASK IS NOT REFUSING ANYTHING. HE HAS A CAN, OR A DRUM, OR A BAG, OR A ROUTE, AND HE IS IN A HURRY. A CONTRADICTION REQUIRES A SECOND VISIT. A SECOND VISIT IS A DECISION. NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS REQUIRED TO DECIDE ANYTHING AT ALL. THE DRIFT IS INVISIBLE FROM INSIDE THAT ROOM AND IT IS INVISIBLE FOR A REASON NOBODY WANTS TO HEAR, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE ONLY PEOPLE WHO COULD CONTRADICT A STATE ARE THE PEOPLE WHO HAVE ALREADY ASKED ONCE.**

**AND THE FUTURE, STATED OUT LOUD TWICE IN CHAPTERS 0136 AND 0138 AND IT IS THE THING THE BATCH IS BUILDING TOWARDS: A REGISTER THAT GROWS WHEN NOBODY IS HURT IS A REGISTER SOMEBODY CAN HOLD OVER YOU. A DRAWER OF SLIPS GROWS EXACTLY THE SAME WAY. OUT OF CORRECT THINGS DONE BY CAREFUL PEOPLE. NOBODY IS HURT BY IT. IT GROWS AT THE RATE OF A PERSON WALKING THROUGH A DOOR AND ASKING A QUESTION THAT SOMEBODY IS NOT REQUIRED TO ASK. **THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE REGISTER AND THE DRAWER IS ONE LINE LONG: NOBODY EVER WROTE A RULE FOR THE PERSON.** The register has nineteen entries and a blank line under the nineteenth and no rule about who may write under the nineteenth. The drawer has no line. Not a blank one. A PERSON HAS NO LINE AT ALL. And the ninth seat is not told any of this and is not going to be.

**AND TWO DRAWERS IN TWO VEHICLES THAT BELONG TO NOBODY WHO IS KEEPING THEM, both growing, and in about four years somebody in this city is going to be able to say how many, and how many is a capacity, and a capacity is a promise, and the cutting will not be done by anybody cruel. It will be done by a number. Nobody has to cut anything. The number does it by existing.**

**AND THE HOOK, AND IT IS NOW A STATED FINDING AND NOT A HOOK: A SLIP IN A DRAWER IS GOING TO BE EVIDENCE ONE DAY. NOT HIS EVIDENCE. A PIECE OF PAPER THAT SOMEBODY KEPT BECAUSE THEY COULD NOT THINK WHAT ELSE TO DO WITH IT, HANDED OVER BY A PERSON WHO THINKS THEY ARE HELPING. And there is no version of that piece of paper in which the person it was written for is in it, because they were not, because they are never in it, because there is no name box and there is not going to be one. And nobody is going to be able to say afterwards whether it was a service or a choice, and neither is he.**

## 4. FINDABILITY, AND THE REFUSAL TO USE HIS OWN METHOD, AND THE MAN AT THE BOARD OF FORTY SLOTS

**THE MAN WHO TURNS THE BUCKET AT THE BOARD OF FORTY SLOTS IS ONE OF THE SIX LOWLAND WATER POINTS. It is a stand with a bucket on a chain and a board of forty slots at a bus turning head, and it works because a man puts money in the slot and takes the bucket and washes it and puts it back, and the man who runs it could not tell you his name either, and that sentence was said out loud in a room in daylight **on Tuesday the thirteenth of January 2015** by Abu Bakayoko, fifty-eight, and it is still the whole of what anybody knows. **The fourteenth of January is not a date anything in this account happens on, and the sentence is his and not Jonas Mercer's.** HE IS NOT FINDABLE FROM ANY RECORD IN THIS CITY AND HAS NEVER BEEN, and there is no party, no reference, no holder field, no name box, no return, no rota, no minute and no form on which his name could be written, and the reason there is no record of him is not that he was missed. It is that nothing in this borough has ever had to write down a man who turns a bucket.**

**AND THE STAND IS IN A MINUTE. The six lowland water points are in paragraph 6.1 of the minute of 19 May at Tier 1, £11,280 a year, recorded as received and not as evidence, and a green pillar with a bucket on a chain and a board of forty slots is a shape in a paragraph with a number in it, and a man in a corridor in a haversack in about nine seconds could go from that paragraph to a bus turning head and stand there, and there would be a man in front of him every day for as long as the pillar stands. NOBODY WOULD HAVE TO SPEND ELEVEN SECONDS. THE PRICE ALREADY DID IT.**

**AND THE FINDING OF CHAPTER 0132, AND IT RECASTS THE THIRTEENTH OF MARCH WITHOUT RESTATING IT: FINDABILITY IS NOT A THING THIS BOROUGH HAS BEEN MINTING. FINDABILITY IS WHAT A PRICE DOES WHEN THERE IS NO COUNTER IN FRONT OF IT. A COUNTER IS THE CHEAPEST PRIVACY DEVICE ANYBODY IN THIS CITY HAS EVER BUILT AND IT COST NOTHING AND NOBODY DESIGNED IT AND THERE IS NO FORM FOR IT: there are three feet of wood between a person and a person, and a man can come in off the street with a payment or a complaint and be answered by somebody he cannot see past, and nothing about him is required to go anywhere. THE MAN AT THE BOARD OF FORTY SLOTS HAS NO WALL, BECAUSE HE HAS TO TAKE THE MONEY, AND HE IS THE MOST FINDABLE MAN IN THE LOWLAND AND HAS BEEN FOR TWENTY-SIX YEARS AND NOBODY DID IT.**

**AND THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT HE HAS REFUSED TO USE HIS OWN METHOD, STATED OUT LOUD IN A SHOP ON FRIDAY 20 MARCH 2015, GIVEN TO BEATRICE OSUNDE, WHO DID NOT ARGUE WITH IT AND DID NOT IMPROVE IT: HE DID NOT GO TO THE BUS TURNING HEAD. Three ways of going, and every one of them is a service: (1) ask the man his name, which makes a man findable; (2) describe the stand to somebody, which puts a shape in a corridor; (3) stand there, which makes the finder into the handle. **THE FINDER IS THE HANDLE. THE CHEAPEST HANDLE IN THIS CITY IS NOT A DATE. IT IS A PERSON WALKING UP TO A PILLAR AND BEING HANDED A BUCKET. AND THE MOST EXPENSIVE THING ANYBODY CAN DO TO A MAN WHO ALREADY HAS ONE IS TO GO AND INTRODUCE HIMSELF.** A priced-access case is not a recognition case. Being seen because you charge is not being recognised, and a record that put him in it as a person would be a record of a price, and if the price came down the record would be wrong and nobody could tell. HE DID NOT GO ON THE WEDNESDAY, THE THURSDAY OR THE FRIDAY, and nothing in that week said a man had chosen anything. THE STAND WENT ON WORKING, THE WATER WENT ON COSTING WHAT IT COSTS, THE MAN WENT ON BEING FINDABLE, NOBODY WAS HELPED, NOBODY WAS HURT, AND THE SIXTH OF THE SIX IS STILL NOT NAMED IN ANY DOCUMENT THAT LEAVES THE STREET.**

**AND ON FRIDAY 20 APRIL 2015 THE PRICE OF FINDABILITY CAME BACK AT HIM FOR THE FIRST TIME, IN HIS OWN PERSON, AND IT IS THE SECOND MOUTH OF THE THIRTEENTH OF MARCH. A woman of about thirty came into that vestibule and asked NINA CALDER, in front of him, at the wall, four feet away: `Is the man who stands at the wall on a list.` She was told no, in about four seconds, and she was told the second half as well, which is that he is right and it does not help her, and there is no form on any counter in this building that would take her question, and if there were one then in about four years there would be a list of people who stand at walls. She said `That's a shame` and went out into the street and did not come back. **THE COUNTER WAS RIGHT. A COUNTER THAT ANSWERS ABOUT A PERSON IS A SERVICE. JONAS MERCER STOOD AT THAT WALL FOR ABOUT NINE MINUTES AND SAID NOTHING, AND THERE WAS NO POINT AT WHICH HE COULD HAVE SAID ANYTHING, AND THERE IS NO POINT AT WHICH ANYBODY COULD. The price of the floor is being paid in a currency where the only thing anybody can do about it is refuse, and refusing does not make the person safer, it makes them unattacked. He has been living on the difference between those two things for four months and it is the only instrument in this borough that works and IT DOES NOT PROTECT ANYBODY. IT ONLY MEANS NOBODY IS AIMING.**

## 5. WHAT A METHOD DID ON A SUNDAY, AND WHERE IT WENT, AND THAT IT TRAVELS SIDEWAYS

**EMMANUEL OTIENO, 38, IS PERMITTED A CLOSE POV IN CHAPTER 0133 AND WAS GIVEN ONE. Wednesday 25 March 2015, about two in the afternoon, a kitchen on the top floor of a building on a road he has never seen the name of on any paper, one window, a yard, a table with two chairs, a plate in the sink with the pattern worn through in the middle, and a daughter of nine at school until half past three who comes in on the left foot first and puts her shoes on wrong, and if the shoes are not by the door she does them on the pavement. He put them by the door.**

**AND HERE IS WHAT HE DID WITH A THING HE WORKED OUT ALONE, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH TAUGHT HIM IT AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS ABLE TO TELL HIM WHAT TO DO WITH IT. He gave it away. Three times. And he wrote nothing down and told nobody and there is no form in this borough on which anybody could record that a man of thirty-eight taught three people a thing he worked out himself.**

1. **A woman of about thirty-one at the depot**, four years, up two nights running with a mother in a block of flats, who asked him on a Tuesday in February how he knew a thing was true on a day, and he told her, and she wrote nothing down either, and he was prouder of that than of anything he has done.
2. **A man of about fifty-five on the second floor of that building**, who does not work shifts and is on no list anybody has ever seen, who asked him in that kitchen on a Sunday in the middle of March why he was so calm about a landlord, and asked him to say it again in a different way, and he did, twice.
3. **A man about thirty he had met once, in a queue outside a hospital, in the middle of February, over a broken coffee machine, who had been at the same school in a different decade, and who had a daughter too, and who had written a date on the back of his hand and asked him whether that counted. It counted. That was the first time anybody had asked him that. He did not tell him the half about a rent book and is not going to.**

**AND HE HAS A PLASTIC WALLET IN THE GLOVEBOX OF A VAN HE DOES NOT OWN, IN A YARD TWO STREETS AWAY, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CAN SAY HOW MANY PIECES OF PAPER ARE IN IT, AND THAT IS CORRECT, AND THE REASON IT IS CORRECT IS THAT HE IS NOT FINDABLE FROM ANY RECORD IN THIS CITY AND HAS NOT ASKED ANYBODY ANYTHING SINCE THE SIXTH OF FEBRUARY. He did not open the glovebox on the Wednesday afternoon, and it is not a thing he is going to start doing, and the reason is that a man who opens a glovebox on a Wednesday afternoon is a man who is looking at it, and a man who is looking at it will open it again.**

**AND HE HAD ALREADY WORKED OUT THE FAR END OF IT, ALONE, IN A KITCHIN, WITH THE TAP RUNNING, IN FEBRUARY, AND TOLD NOBODY. IN ABOUT FOUR YEARS SOMEBODY IS GOING TO WRITE A FORM. The form will be a good form, with a box on it and a reference and a date, and it will say what that counter does, and the woman who hands it over will not have chosen to be in it and will not be able to be un-in it, because a form with a name on it is a duty and a duty cannot be refused after it is printed. AND THE WALL IS NOT THE COUNTER. THE WALL IS THE DAY SOMEBODY CAN SAY *WE CAN ONLY DO EIGHT TODAY* AND BE ENTIRELY CORRECT, and the day that can be said is the day the room is a room with a service in it, and it will not be the man who said it. It will never be the man who said it. It will be the first person who is tired and honest.**

**AND IT TRAVELS SIDEWAYS, WHICH IS THE FINDING OF CHAPTER 0133, AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME IN NINE MONTHS THAT ANYTHING HAS COME OUT OF THAT COUNTER AND TOUCHED A DISTRICT. It did not go upwards — not to a manager, not to a committee, not to a records office, not to a board of nine seats with two chairs empty. It went to a woman on a shift, and a man on a second floor, and a man in a queue, and from a woman on a shift to a girl on a till, and from a girl on a till to a kitchen on the other side of this borough, and every step of that is a person telling a person at a kettle or in a queue or in a doorway, and not one of the steps is a document, and not one of the steps could be produced by anybody, and there is no instrument in this city that can see any of it.**

**AND WHAT A MAN OF THIRTY-FOUR IN A CANTEEN SAID AGAINST A WALL AT ABOUT HALF PAST FIVE ON WEDNESDAY 25 MARCH, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF THE BATCH: `It's not strange any more, that's all I wanted. There's a girl on our till who's had two of them off a landlord and she's not even surprised, she just said oh, they all do that now.`**

**AND WHY THE FEAR WAS THE WRONG FEAR. Jonas Mercer had been afraid of a form since 4 September and he was right to be and it is not going to happen. WHAT HAS HAPPENED INSTEAD IS THAT IT STOPPED BEING A THING ANYBODY IS DOING. A DISCOVERY HAS BECOME WEATHER. The way you protect a thing like that from being written down is to make sure nobody can describe it, and a man of thirty-eight made sure it could be described, on purpose, out loud, three times, to three people, and nobody in this borough taught him that and nobody in this borough can tell him what to do with it.**

**AND JONAS MERCER ASKED HIS ONE QUESTION OF THE BATCH AND IT WAS SIX WORDS AND IT WAS IN A CORRIDOR AND A CORRIDOR IS A CORRIDOR AND HE KNEW THAT WHEN HE ASKED IT: `And who else has got it.` Three that the man knew of, and more than that by now, and no form for it, and nobody is going to put it on paper. AND HE IS NOT GOING TO GO AND ASK HIM, AND THE REASON IS EIGHT WORDS AND IT GOES IN A PAD AND NOWHERE ELSE: **I AM THE PERSON WHO MADE IT CHEAP. The first time I ask him a question about it, he is a person somebody can ask about, and I have spent nine months refusing to make doors out of people, and I am not going to make one out of the only man in this borough who worked something out on his own and gave it away for nothing.**

**AND ONE OF THE THREE WORKS SOMEWHERE WITH A NAME. The man in the corridor said a name on the Wednesday evening, not slowly and not twice, and Jonas Mercer did not ask him to say it again, and it is a name that is on the drawing layer in this city with a filled square beside it and an expiry and a node number, because eight of the nine shapes on that layer have names and a filled square and the ninth has not got one and never will. **HE DOES NOT KNOW WHICH ONE OF THE THREE IT IS AND HE IS NOT GOING TO FIND OUT, and there is no form in this borough on which he could ask, and asking is how a discovery becomes a finding, and a finding goes in a report, and a report is a thing a person can be held to.** NOBODY WAS HELPED, NOBODY WAS HARMED, NOTHING WAS RESOLVED, AND NOTHING WAS WRITTEN DOWN.**

## 6. THE A WOMAN OF THIRTY-FOUR, TWICE ASKED, AND DID NOT COME, AND THE FOUR LINES

**THE ATTRIBUTION IS NOW FIXED AND IS BINDING, BECAUSE TWO EARLIER DOCUMENTS GOT IT WRONG. JONAS MERCER DID NOT WRITE THE FOUR LINES AND NEVER DID AND HAS NEVER CLAIMED THEM.**

- **WHAT HE DID WAS SAY A NAME OUT LOUD, on Wednesday the third of December 2014, at about twenty to seven in the evening, in a room with about eleven people in it, in about nine seconds.** The minute of that evening says that a name was stated. It does not contain the name. It cannot be produced, argued with, minuted, published, attached to a claim, or found by anybody who was not one of the about eleven people in that room, and there is no list of who was in that room and there is not going to be one.
- **THE FOUR LINES AT THE TOP OF THAT SHEET OF A4 ARE THE MINUTE-TAKER'S. They are in biro. They were written on Wednesday the twenty-first of January 2015 in about four minutes, on a second sheet that had nothing at the top of it when she took it. Underneath them, in a different hand, are four lines that are not hers and are nobody else's, and nobody has said out loud in a room that those four lines came from the woman, and nobody in this borough is going to say it.**
- **NO CHAPTER MAY PUT HIS HAND TO THE PAPER OR THE PEN, AND HE HAS NOT AND WILL NOT.** On 24 December, on a bench in a shop, Beatrice Osunde told him the rule and he has kept it every day since: *You have been writing things down since April for the people in the room. That last one is yours. Do not lose it and do not show it to anybody, and there is no box on it anywhere and that is also the point.*
- **The other piece of paper is a letter, in a handbag, in a kitchen off a landing. Nobody in this borough has been in that kitchen, and it has not been opened, and it is not going to be, and it is not a document.**

**AND THERE IS NO NUMBER IN THIS BOROUGH FOR ANYBODY TO TELEPHONE, AND IT IS NOT ON A LIST, AND IT IS NOT GOING ON ONE, AND THE REASON IS FOUR WORDS LONG:**

> **NOBODY OWNS THAT NUMBER.**

**A LIST OF TELEPHONE NUMBERS IS A LIST OF PEOPLE. A LIST OF PEOPLE WHO CANNOT BE REACHED IS A LIST OF PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT IN A ROOM. A BODY OF NINE SEATS CANNOT REQUIRE A PERSON TO DO ANYTHING, NOT A FORM, NOT A SIGNATURE, NOT A TELEPHONE CALL, AND NOT TO ATTEND A SITTING IT IS NOT REQUIRED TO HOLD, and the seven people in those seats have not met since the middle of January and are not going to meet in April. NOBODY CAN MAKE HER COME, AND NOBODY CAN EVEN MAKE ANYBODY TRY TO MAKE HER COME, because a body cannot require a person to do anything, including the thing that would require the person to be required to do anything first, and that is not a paradox anybody in this borough has solved and it is not going to be solved.**

**AND NOTHING HAPPENED. Four months, two rooms, in daylight, with papers. The printed extract from Committee Services went back into a tray in a hall in Tideglass on Monday 30 March at about eleven o'clock, and the putting back took a woman about four seconds, and the putting back is the only thing anybody in this borough has done about that person in four months. HER NAME IS NOT ON IT. THERE IS NO NAME BOX ON IT. IT HAS NEVER HAD HER NAME ON IT AND IT IS NOT GOING TO BE PUT ON IT, AND THERE IS NO INSTRUMENT IN THIS CITY BY WHICH ANYBODY COULD PUT A NAME ON A PIECE OF PAPER THAT HAS NO NAME BOX.**

**AND THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE ONLY HONEST THING ANYBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS PRODUCED ABOUT A PERSON IN NINE MONTHS: A HOLE IN THE RECORD IS THE ONLY HONEST THING. Everything else this borough has produced in nine months is a thing — a sentence, a state, a date, a register with a blank line under it, a form with no name box, a chair that does not exist, a term read aloud in a room with four chairs in it. This is the only one that is an absence, and the absence is a person, and it is the only one nobody can use.**

**AND THE PRICE, WHICH IS EXACT, AND NOBODY HAD WORKED IT OUT BEFORE: THE MOST EXPENSIVE THING ANYBODY IN THIS CITY HAS PRODUCED ABOUT A PERSON IN NINE MONTHS IS A PIECE OF A4 IN A DRAWER WITH NO KEY ON IT, AND NOBODY IS GOING TO OPEN IT, AND THE PRICE OF THAT PIECE OF PAPER IS THAT A WOMAN OF THIRTY-FOUR IS A PERSON THIS BOROUGH CAN SAY NOTHING ABOUT AT ALL. Not nothing nearly. Nothing at all. No claim, no reference, no return, no field, no counter, no list, no form, no minute, no slip, no extract, no envelope with a departmental reference, and no telephone number, and there is no route to her that is not a document, and every one of the five documents that exist is a document that cannot be produced by anybody she has not spoken to. **AND THAT IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME, IT IS NOT A CONSOLATION, AND THERE IS NO ARGUMENT IN THIS BOROUGH IN WHICH IT COULD BE MADE BETTER BY ANYBODY DOING MORE.**

**AND THE ONE DRAWNER WITH NO KEY IS THE ONLY HONEST THING ABOUT HER, WHICH IS TWELVE WORDS AND IS NOT A PROMISE AND IS NOT ON A PAD.**

## 7. A REASON, GIVEN TO SOMEBODY WITH A PEN, AND WHO KEEPS THE MINUTES

**THE WOMAN WHO KEEPS THE MINUTES IS THE SAME PERSON WHO STANDS AT THAT COUNTER, AND THAT IS NOW CANON, AND IT WAS ESTABLISHED IN CHAPTER 0136 AND JONAS MERCER TOOK TEN WEEKS TO WORK IT OUT BECAUSE HE HAD BEEN ASSUMING THERE WAS A BOX SOMEWHERE THAT SAID SO.**

- **There is no box.** There is a sheet that says *minute taken by* and there is a name in it and that is the only name-box on the whole of the ground floor. **The sheet is the minute until about four o'clock and after that it is only a sheet**, and she is the only person in this city who can end a minute by picking one up and putting it down.
- **If there were a box that tied *minute taken by* to *counter, ground floor*, that would be a rota with one name in it, and the name would be hers, and the rota would be the establishment of a service floor in a building, by a person, in about eleven seconds, and it would be the only thing anybody in this borough has actually wanted since the fourth of September.**
- **She is not on the board and not on a rota and is not going to be on either. She is about fifty, has nineteen years in that office, designing lists since 1999, and comes down at about ten and about three because nobody has ever told her to and nobody could.**

**AND ON WEDNESDAY 8 APRIL 2015, IN DAYLIGHT, IN A ROOM WITH ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE IN IT, SHE SAID A SENTENCE ABOUT HERSELF. NOBODY ASKED HER. IT TOOK ABOUT ELEVEN SECONDS. IT IS NOT A REASON AGAINST A REGISTER ENTRY AND IT IS NOT GOING ON A SLIP.**

> **I DECIDE IT, AND THERE IS NOBODY I AM ALLOWED TO ASK WHETHER I HAVE DECIDED IT RIGHT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF IT, AND I HAVE HAD THAT FOR NINETEEN YEARS.**

**AND WHAT SHE HAD DONE, AND IT IS THE FINDING OF CHAPTER 0136: SHE DID NOT SAY IT TO HIM. SHE SAID IT TO THE ROOM. A SENTENCE SAID TO ONE PERSON IN A CORRIDOR IS A THING TWO PEOPLE KNOW AND IT CAN BE USED AND IT BELONGS TO THE TWO OF THEM — a porter said that to a man with a trolley on 2 March and he was exactly right, and a man of thirty-four in a canteen in March said the other side of it: a thing that is said in a room is a thing a room knows. **THERE IS NO BOX ON A ROOM.** No form in this borough has a room on it, no return, no field, no reference, no index and no rota, and a vestibule eleven feet by nine full of people on a Wednesday morning in April is not an establishment and cannot be interrogated. She chose the room because a room cannot be asked what happened in it and a corridor can, and a corridor is where a man asks a porter a question. A person who has been refusing things for nineteen years has had nobody ask her for a reason, and a person who has never been asked for a reason does not know whether her reasons are any good, and the only way to find out whether a sentence is true is to say it out loud where it can be overheard.**

**AND THE OTHER HALF, WHICH IS THE REASON, AND IT IS ABOUT NINE SECONDS: she said it to him and not to the wall because he has had a pen since 4 September and has been writing down why other people say no for nine months, and nobody in this city has ever once asked him for one of his, and she found out in about four minutes on the Wednesday morning that she had got one, and had never told anybody that she did not have one until he handed it to her by not asking.**

**HE WROTE IT DOWN, IN ABOUT FOUR SECONDS, ON THE LEFT-HAND PAGE OF A PAD, IN A CORRIDOR, BECAUSE THERE WAS NO MINUTE — THE BOARD WAS NOT SITTING AND IS NOT REQUIRED TO. She saw him do it. She put her pen down, which is the thing she does about four times a year, and said: `Nobody in this borough has ever written down one of mine. You are going to. And it is going in a book that goes in a shop at the end of a street and it is not going anywhere, and I know that, and I am letting it, and do not come back and tell me what you did with it.`**

**AND THE CONSEQUENCES, ALL OF THEM, AND NONE OF THEM MAY BE UNDONE IN CHAPTERS 141–144:**

1. **THAT SENTENCE IS NOW IN ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE AND IN NO DOCUMENT, and that is precisely the thing she refused on 2 January, and it has happened anyway, and it was not anybody's fault, and nobody in this borough did it to her, and she went into that room on purpose and had worked out on the way in what she was going to do.**
2. **NOBODY MAY ASK HER A QUESTION ABOUT IT AFTERWARDS AND NOBODY DID. HE DID NOT ASK HER WHETHER IT WAS GOING IN THE MINUTE AND SHE DID NOT OFFER. FOUR PEOPLE IN THAT ROOM HEARD IT AND TWO OF THEM LOOKED AT HER AND ONE OF THEM SAID `what was that` ABOUT FOUR MINUTES LATER TO SOMEBODY ELSE AND WAS TOLD IT WAS NOTHING, and nothing was the correct answer and it was not a lie. There is no item about the eighth of April in any minute and there is not going to be one.**
3. **IT IS NOW IN ONE HAND IN A BOOK THAT GOES NOWHERE, WHICH IS THE FIRST TIME ANYTHING SHE HAS SAID HAS GONE ANYWHERE AT ALL, AND SHE KNEW THAT WHEN SHE LET HIM DO IT, AND SHE LET IT.** Nobody may open that pad and nobody may ask what is in it. Nobody has asked her about it since and nobody is going to.
4. **M. FURREAUX AND HOWARD BRAMBLE DID NOT ENTER THAT CHAPTER AND MAY NOT BE ARGUED WITH AND MAY NOT COME BACK A THIRD TIME.**
5. **AND SHE IS GOING TO BE PROVED RIGHT ABOUT THE REGISTER, AND IT IS GOING TO BE ABOUT THE SHELF AND NOT ABOUT THE BULB, AND SHE DOES NOT KNOW THAT YET, AND JONAS MERCER DOES AND IS NOT GOING TO TELL HER, and the reason he has written down is that if he told her she would be the woman who was warned.**

**AND HER NINE WORDS WERE SET OUT ONCE, IN CHAPTER 0136, WHERE THE CHAPTER IS ABOUT A SENTENCE BEING GIVEN OUT LOUD, AND NO LATER CHAPTER IN THIS VOLUME MAY RESTATE THEM: a number of what a counter does is a level of service, and the day a floor has a level of service somebody can cut it. And the reason column does not exist and will not exist, and there is still no form on which anybody could write that these are not a series.**

## 8. THE HOUR, AND THE FOUR HUNDRED YARDS, AND WHY HE STOPPED

**THE HOUR BETWEEN SIX AND SEVEN EXISTS ON EVERY SUNDAY AND THREE CHAPTERS STAGED IT AND NOBODY MAY STAGE IT AGAIN WITHOUT A LINE HERE SAYING SO: Chapter 0135, Sunday 5 April 2015 · Chapter 0137, Sunday 12 April 2015 · Chapter 0139, Sunday 26 April 2015. The 26th of April was the fourth of those in four weeks, after the 5th, the 12th and the 19th, and there is no date in this city for any of them and nobody wrote any of them down.**

**AND WHAT A HOUR IS, WHEN A MAN STANDS IN ONE AND IT IS THE ONLY HOUR OF THE WEEK IN WHICH THIS BOROUGH REQUIRES NOTHING OF ANYBODY, WHICH IS THE FINDING OF CHAPTER 0137 AND IS FOUR LINES AND IS NOT GOING ON A WALL: IT IS A FLOOR THAT IS NOT LEVEL, AND THERE IS NOBODY IN IT. A term is a promise made by two tired people at ten o'clock on a Saturday night, and a promise that runs six days and then stops, made by two people who are not on anything, on their own time, with nothing written down, IS THE CHEAPEST THING ANYBODY IN THIS CITY HAS EVER PRODUCED. IN THAT HOUR FOUR HUNDRED AND TWENTY WOMEN ARE NOT ON THE FAR SIDE OF A PARAGRAPH NUMBER, BECAUSE THERE IS NO PARAGRAPH AND NO TERM. IN THAT HOUR THE ELEVEN O'CLOCK TO HALF PAST ONE ROW IS NOT EMPTY, BECAUSE THERE IS NO ROTA AND NO BOARD. IN THAT HOUR THE REGISTER HAS NO NINETEENTH ENTRY WITH A BULB OUT ON IT.**

**AND THE FINDING THAT HE COULD NOT HOLD, WHICH IS THE REAL ONE AND IT IS ABOUT HIM: **THE HOUR CANNOT BE SCHEDULED WITHOUT SOMEBODY BEING REQUIRED TO BE IN IT.** Not a rota. Not a rule. Any schedule at all contains the sentence *somebody will be there*, and a sentence with somebody in it is a requirement, and the registrar put it in a minute in June: a clause that cannot be challenged by a person cannot require them to, and a column with a name in it can be challenged by the person whose name is in it, and a person who is allowed to say no to a column is no longer a column, and then there is nothing on the wall at all. **SO THE ONLY WAY TO KEEP THE HOUR IS TO KEEP IT UNSCHEDULED, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT KEEPS IT UNSCHEDULED IS THE SAME INSTRUMENT THAT HAS BEEN DOING EVERYTHING ELSE FOR NINE MONTHS, WHICH IS TWO PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT ON ANYTHING TURNING UP AT TEN O'CLOCK ON A SATURDAY BECAUSE NOBODY WROTE ANYTHING DOWN. It is the cheapest thing in this borough. It is the only thing that works. There is no instrument for it and there cannot be one and the attempt to make one is the exact moment this whole thing stops.**

**AND FOUR HUNDRED YARDS IS NOT AN ANSWER EITHER, AND THAT IS THE FINDING OF CHAPTERS 0135, 0137 AND 0139 TOGETHER. The four hundred yards is a piece of wet pavement at a bus turning head, and he has stood on it five times since December. In late December, in the dark. On 3 January 2015, in the rain, at ten o'clock. On 14 March 2015 at ten o'clock, deliberately. On 3 April 2015 at about twenty past six in the morning. On 11 April 2015 at ten past ten at night. **FROM FOUR HUNDRED YARDS YOU CANNOT TELL WHETHER A DOOR IS OPEN OR SHUT, AND THAT IS THE CORRECT AMOUNT OF EVIDENCE.** What it buys is that he cannot be a rota, could not be expected, could not be noticed, could not be seen to be there, could not be asked whether he had been, and could not be a reason that a porter began to look at a corridor. And that stopped being true by the eleventh of April, because four hundred yards had been safe on 3 April only because on 3 April it was a decision he had made on the Friday, and then he stood on the same pavement on the eleventh at about ten past ten at night for about half an hour and worked out that **four hundred yards is a place, and a place a man goes to is the first half of a schedule, and a schedule is a rota with one name in it, and a man who is regularly four hundred yards away is a man who is regularly four hundred yards away.** He stood in the corridor instead, on the Sunday morning at about twenty past six, which was the second time he had ever stood in a corridor on a Sunday morning. **He has stood in one exactly twice, at half past four in the morning on 4 January 2015 and at twenty past six in the morning on 12 April 2015, and the first of those had not been planned for a week and the second one had, and that is the whole of the difference.**

**AND THE MOVE HE HAS NOT MADE AND IS NOT GOING TO MAKE IN CHAPTERS 141–144 WITHOUT A LINE HERE SAYING SO: HE DID NOT OPEN ANYTHING. The claim to open a door in this volume was spent on 28 January 2015 in a room in daylight in about four seconds, and it is the only thing he has ever spent in nine months, and he was not going to go back to a thing he has already spent because it would make the next four days easier. THERE WAS NOTHING IN THAT CORRIDOR HE WAS ALLOWED TO OPEN AND HE OPENED NOTHING AND THERE WAS NO MOMENT IN THE WHOLE OF THE HOUR WHEN HE WANTED TO.**

**AND THE THING THE BATCH ENDS ON, WHICH IS ABOUT HIM AND IS THE FIRST TIME, AND IT IS THE SECOND MOUTH OF EVERYTHING: **HE HAS BEEN DOING IT FOR NOTHING FOR FOUR MONTHS AND THE ENTIRE PRODUCT IS THAT TWO TIRED MEN COULD SAY THAT HE WAS THERE.** That is all. And he has worked out that he would rather be that than a name on a list. **AND THAT IS NOT A PRINCIPLE. IT IS A PRICE.** And there is a difference and he knows exactly what it is, because he has been in a room in daylight on 28 January and has said out loud what a thing like that is worth and it is nothing that anybody can be held to. And Beatrice Osunde told him in December that a thing like that has to be said to somebody four times a day for a week before it holds, **AND HE HAS SAID IT TO HER ONCE, ON MONDAY THE THIRTEENTH OF APRIL 2015, AND HE CAME IN AGAIN ON THE TWENTY-FOURTH WITH THE SAME THING IN HIS MOUTH AND DID NOT SAY IT, and that is the first time in nine months he has come into that shop with a sentence in him and gone out without it, and the reason is not that he has changed his mind. THE REASON IS THAT A THING THAT HAS BEEN SAID ONCE HAS NOT BEEN TESTED, AND A THING THAT HAS NOT BEEN TESTED IS A PREFERENCE. HE IS NOT GOING TO ASK HER AGAIN, HE IS NOT GOING TO ANYBODY ELSE WITH IT, AND NOBODY IS GOING TO BE TOLD. And on the twenty-fourth she said: `The oil came in on Tuesday and the tin is by the door and I would like it moved before the weekend. And that is not the same conversation and I am telling you that it is not the same conversation so that you know I know it is not the same conversation.`**

## 0. WHAT THE CLOSE WAS FOR, AND WHAT IT DID NOT DO

The close had to do three things an ordinary batch does not: close the volume's central pressure, leave the standing threads unresolved, and hand the reader to Volume 04 with a question and not a resolution.

**THE CENTRAL PRESSURE OF VOLUME 03, IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS: A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO IS HELPED, AND A SERVICE IN THIS BOROUGH HAS ONLY EVER BEEN AVAILABLE TO A PERSON SOMEBODY PUT IN A FIELD, AND A FIELD IS A BOX, AND THE BOX IS WHERE THE NAME WOULD GO.** The volume's own work in the last four days was the consequence of the three answers, of which nobody had been made to live under any. **Chapter 0141 staged the consequence of the first answer and it was a person. Chapter 0142 staged the consequence of the second answer and it was a landing. Chapter 0143 staged the consequence of the third answer and it was a corridor. Chapter 0144 said the whole of it out loud in a room in daylight and then could not finish it, because the part of it with people in it has nowhere to go.** In all four of them a person was told a correct thing by somebody who was not required to give it, and nobody was helped, nobody was harmed, nothing was resolved, and nothing was written down.

**WHAT THE CLOSE DID NOT DO, AND NONE OF IT MAY BE UNDONE IN VOLUME 04 WITHOUT A LINE HERE SAYING SO: it did not dissolve anything, grant anything, fix anything, or move a person out of a place they cannot afford. It did not improve him. He was not given a title, a grade, a department, a chair, a seat, a membership, a form, a rota row, a thank-you, or a way of being thanked, and nobody thanked him for anything, and no character said out loud that they had not been thanked and were not going to be, and the ninth seat is not thanked for anything. He did not say a fourth answer and nobody asked him a fourth question. He asked no question of anybody in any of the four chapters and has now asked none since the twenty-fifth of February 2015. He did not open anything. He did not resolve the drift, the shelf, the compliance paragraph, the hand that puts the strip in the drawer, Royden Achebe, Peter Naylor, the man of forty-eight, the woman of thirty-four, the man of thirty-eight, the lowland's missing seat, Tomas Renn's question, the letter of 18 February, the card in the slot, or Prue Calloway's finding, and all of them are open and live.**

## 0a. THE DAY-COUNTS AT THE END OF THE CLOSE, RECOMPUTED FROM THE THREE ANCHORS AND NEVER FROM A FIGURE CARRIED FORWARD IN A SUMMARY

- **THE BLANK LINE UNDER THE NINETEENTH, since Wednesday 26 November 2014. 110 · 114 · 121 · 124 · 133 · 145 · 149 · 151 · 154 in Chapters 131–140, and then 155 (Thu 30 April) · 156 (Fri 1 May) · 157 (Sat 2 May) · A HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT (Wed 13 May 2015).** That is the longest it has ever been still since the fourth of August, and it is the only fixed point in the building, and it is the single most load-bearing object in Volume 03. **The volume ends with it blank.**
- **THE CARD IN THE SLOT, since Friday 20 February 2015. 69 (30 April) · 70 (1 May) · 71 (2 May) · EIGHTY-TWO (13 May 2015).** Nobody has taken it out and nobody has put it up and Nina Calder has not read it and is not going to.
- **THE LETTER IN THE TRAY, since Wednesday 18 February 2015 at about half past nine. 71 (30 April) · 72 (1 May) · 73 (2 May) · EIGHTY-FOUR (13 May 2015).** It is still sealed, has not been opened in front of a second person, has not been told about, has not been answered, and what is under the post on top of it is not known to anybody in this account and may not be stated in a room or in a document. **No chapter in this volume opened it and no chapter in Volume 04 may open it without a line here saying so.**

## 1. CHAPTER 0141 — THURSDAY 30 APRIL 2015 — THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE FIRST ANSWER, AND IT IS A PERSON

**FOUR PIECES OF PAPER IN THIS BOROUGH MENTION THE TROUGH BY THE LOCK-UPS, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM IS TRUE, AND NOT ONE OF THEM CAN BE PRODUCED BY ANYBODY, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THE CHAPTER IS ABOUT.** The oldest is dated 26 January and mentions it in a line between four others and went into the inside pocket of the man with the bowser in the rain and has not been looked at once. The second is dated the second of February and mentions nothing else. The third is dated the thirteenth of February and mentions nothing else. **ALL THREE OF THOSE ARE IN THE SAME INSIDE POCKET IN THE SAME COAT, and the man has not stood in that room since the middle of February, and there is no reason he would come back, and he is right not to come back.** The fourth is dated the sixteenth of March, is about the second of February, and is in the inside pocket of a man with a galvanised can who has never been in that vestibule in his life and who came once more on the twentieth of April to ask whether a piece of paper was a receipt and was told no and put it back in the coat where it had been and has not been back. **So there is no way in this city to ask which of them is the state of the trough, because a state is a person's account of a thing at ten past ten on a day, and there are two men, and they are both right, and neither of them may be required to answer anything, including a correction.**

**THE MAN WITH THE VAN, AND HE IS NEW, AND HE IS NOT THE MAN WITH THE BOWSER AND NOT THE MAN OF ABOUT SIXTY, AND HE HAS NEVER BEEN IN THAT VESTIBULE IN HIS LIFE. A man of about forty-five, in a driver's coat, with a cardboard wallet and grease on the side of the second finger of his right hand. He has THREE pieces of paper in the wallet, about four inches by two, folded once, with a date on each and a hand on each and nothing else on any of them, and he has had them SINCE ABOUT CHRISTMAS.** He asked, in five questions of which the shortest was three words, whether there is a list. **She did not answer any of the five, and she was right about all five, and the answer is the correct one and is the only thing she is entitled to do with a piece of paper in that room, and no duration is given for it and none may be:** she cannot tell him whose they are, she could not if she wanted to, she is not going to work it out, there is nothing on them to work it out from, and no box is going to be on them. There is no list of them and there is not a list of people, and she is not able to write one, and there is nowhere in this borough to write one, and that is not an oversight, and if there were somewhere to write one then in about four years somebody would be able to look one up and the first thing anybody would do with a list like that is find out whether a person is on it and the second thing anybody would do is ask that person how they feel about being on it. Nobody is going to make him keep them and nobody is going to make him throw them away either, and those are the same sentence. He understood it in about four seconds, which is the only time in nine months that anybody has watched a person at that counter be told no and be told why at the same time and come out holding a different idea of what is on the other side of the counter. `So they are not mine.` `They are not yours. And they are not not-yours, and that is the half I cannot help you with.` **He put them back in the inside of his coat and went out and he is going to go on carrying them, and nobody was helped and nobody was harmed.**

**THE FINDING, AND IT IS A FINDING AND NOT A HOOK: A STATE WITH NO OWNER AND NO PERSON ATTACHED TO IT HAS NOW BEEN CARRIED BY A MAN FOR ABOUT THREE MONTHS, AND NOBODY IN THIS CITY CAN TELL WHAT IT IS GOING TO BECOME, AND THE ANSWER IS NOTHING, BECAUSE THERE IS NO INSTRUMENT, AND THAT IS CORRECT.** And it is the answer the trough gave him in January and the answer the corridor gave him in February and he has been given it four times and has not improved it once. **NO FORM WAS WRITTEN IN THAT ROOM ON THAT THURSDAY MORNING, NOBODY ASKED THE COUNTER WHAT A STATE IS, AND THE COUNTER DID NOT USE THE WORD FOR HERSELF IN THAT ROOM.**

**THE ROUTINE, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE CHAPTER. A piece of paper in an inside pocket has become a thing with a routine. A routine with one man in it is a rota. Nobody wrote the rota.** He worked out in April, in a corridor, with a porter, that he could not stop it, and all three ways were closed — he cannot ask the man to stop coming, because a man may not be required to answer anything; he cannot put it in writing, because a paragraph in a corridor is a form and the man who gives it is the man who wrote it; and a man who is regularly four hundred yards away is a man who is regularly four hundred yards away. **Nobody in that room knows what day anybody comes, and he is not going to tell them, and he is not going to be asked, and he would rather it stayed a coincidence.**

**AND HE LOOKED AT THE TROUGH, AND HE WROTE NOTHING DOWN, AND THE REASON IS THREE SENTENCES LONG AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT IS WRONG WITH NINE MONTHS: if he had written a second state about the same trough and it had not agreed with the first two, there would be a contradiction, and a contradiction can only be moved by going back to the men, and the men may not be required to answer anything, including a correction — so the third piece of paper would have been a thing in this borough that could never be moved by anybody, ever, and he would have been the one who put it there. A THING CAN BE LOOKED AT AGAIN. That is the closest this borough gets to a correction, and it has no form in it, and it costs nothing, and it binds nobody, and there is no instrument anywhere that could go and record that a man stood over a trough on a Thursday morning and saw a thing that was not there in February. AND THE ONLY THING HE IS ABLE TO DO ABOUT A WRONG STATEMENT IN THIS CITY IS LOOK AT THE THING IT IS ABOUT, and he did it, and there is no way on earth of writing down that he did.**

## 2. CHAPTER 0142 — FRIDAY 1 MAY 2015 — THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE SECOND ANSWER, AND THE PRICE ARRIVING ON A LANDING

**THE ASKING WAS ON A LANDING IN A BLOCK OF FLATS AND NOT IN THE VESTIBULE ELEVEN FEET BY NINE, AND JONAS MERCER WAS NOT IN IT, WAS NOT GOING TO BE, WAS TOLD NOTHING ABOUT IT, AND IS NEVER GOING TO KNOW IT HAPPENED.** He was in the vestibule that Friday morning for a quarter of an hour, standing at the east end of the counter with his back to the wall, and nobody asked him anything, and a woman of about fifty came down at about ten with a tray, and neither of them said one word to the other. **AND HE WORKED OUT, STANDING THERE, THE THING THAT ROOM HAS NEVER BEEN ASKED AND THAT HE WAS NOT GOING TO ASK IT EITHER: THE ENTIRE MECHANISM RUNS ON PEOPLE BEING IN THE SAME PLACE AT THE SAME HOUR EVERY MORNING. None of it works because anybody built it, and all of it works because the same faces come past it in the same order on the same day. He has stood at that wall on Fridays since the twenty-eighth of January and has never once asked who else comes at ten, and if he asked it would be the first question anybody in nine months had asked in there about a person and it would be about all of them at once, and a question about all of them at once is a register.**

**A WOMAN OF ABOUT SIXTY, UNNAMED, WHO HAS BEEN IN THAT CORRIDOR EVERY MORNING SINCE ABOUT THE BEGINNING OF LAST SUMMER, WHICH IS ABOUT A YEAR, AND HAS NEVER ONCE BEEN ASKED ABOUT IT.** The eleven o'clock to half past one row is empty and is not shaded and does not say *vacant*, and there is a Thursday in a porter's own handwriting that says NO with a second line under it in somebody else's hand, and a card in a plastic sleeve on the Friday row and the Saturday row because somebody put it there herself. **She does not know what any of it means and she has never said a word about it to anybody, and it is not a comfort and she has not been treating it as one. It is just a board that has been there longer than she has.**

At about a quarter to eleven on the second landing there was a man of about thirty with a plastic folder under his arm and a card of his own, and he asked her, in eight words, **whether the board is hers.** He was not a threat, he was not impatient, and he was not cruel: he had been told to leave the card somewhere in the building, there was a man coming on the Monday to take a floor up and he had to be honest about the noise, and a man at work had said that there was a woman in the corridor at the clinic every morning who would know who to give it to, and had not said what her name was.

**The answer was no. And the reason it is no is that nobody may be required to be told anything, and the reason that is the reason is that a person who has been asked about a job is a person who is on something, and a person on something cannot get off it again — and because there is no list anywhere that says she is anything and nowhere in this borough she could be put on one, and that is not an oversight, and because if somebody had asked her in April and had written down that she said no, the writing down would itself have been the asking.** She could not give him anybody to give it to, because she is not anything. She does not know who is on in the mornings either. **He went down the stairs with the card still in his hand and did not leave it on the mat of the flat on the left and did not put it under the door of the flat on the right, and nobody in that building was given a card about a floor being taken up on the Monday. NOBODY WAS HELPED.**

**AND THERE WAS A SECOND PERSON ON THAT LANDING AND SHE SAW THE WHOLE OF IT. A woman going down to the shops with a bag over her wrist came out of her door at the moment he said it, and she stopped, and she said nothing, and she went on down the stairs, and she has not said anything to anybody. That is all being seen to be asked is. It goes nowhere, and it is the only record of it, and there is not going to be another one.**

**THE COST LANDED ON THE PERSON WHO WAS ASKED AND NOT ON THE PERSON WHO ASKED, and it is exact and it is very small.** The man went away with his card in the same pocket, was not angry, did not go away feeling clever, has not thought about it since, and is going to be all right. She has a person established in a building of about thirty flats as the one who is asked, and she did not agree to it, and she cannot be released from it, and **the only instrument anybody in this borough has for releasing anybody from anything is a piece of paper with a name on it, and the one instrument she is not getting is a piece of paper with a name on it, because the absence of her name is the only thing keeping her out of it.** On the Tuesday a man at the bins asked her whether she knew who lived at number four B; on the Thursday a girl on the second landing asked her whether the water was going off at the weekend; both were about thirty seconds long and ordinary; she said no to both and was not thanked for it and was not helped with either. **The only way to stop being asked about the door is to stop being at the door, and the door is the only part of her day she has got, and nobody in this borough is entitled to ask her about the mornings, and she is not going to explain them to anybody.**

**AND THE FINDING, WHICH IS THE SECOND ANSWER COMING BACK A THIRD TIME: THE WHOLE OF WHAT A PRICE DOES IS THAT SOMEBODY ELSE PAYS IT. THE SENTENCE GIVEN OUT LOUD IN THAT ROOM IN MARCH WAS ABOUT FOUR PEOPLE, AND IT WAS CORRECT, AND IT IS STILL CORRECT, AND THERE ARE MORE THAN FOUR, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH HAS AN INSTRUMENT FOR SAYING HOW MANY MORE, AND ADDING THEM UP IS FORBIDDEN, because the first of them is not on a list either and neither is the fifth and there is nowhere to put the answer. NOBODY DIED, NOBODY WAS RESCUED, NOTHING WAS LUCKY, AND NOBODY WAS HELPED.**

## 3. CHAPTER 0143 — SATURDAY 2 MAY 2015, THE MORNING — THE CONSEQUENCE OF THE THIRD ANSWER, COMING BACK FROM OUTSIDE

**A MAN OF THIRTY-THREE WHO WORKS NIGHTS AND HAS BEEN ON NOTHING SINCE HE WAS TWENTY CAME IN ON A SATURDAY MORNING BECAUSE A MAN AT WORK TOLD HIM THERE WAS A MINUTE YOU COULD HAVE, THAT IT WAS FREE, AND THAT YOU DID NOT HAVE TO ASK ANYBODY FOR IT.** The building is open on a Saturday morning for that counter and it has been open for years and nobody has ever written down why; the answer is a car park and a canteen and a man who comes in at nine to do the photocopying and goes at twelve, is not paid for the Saturday, comes anyway, has never been asked to and would not know what to do if he were. **Jonas Mercer had come in on a Saturday for the first time in nine months and had not come for anything, and neither of them knew the other was there for the first twenty minutes of that morning.**

He was given the minute of the twenty-seventh of April, which went out on the Friday, is public, is unsigned, has no crest on it, and **requires no person to do anything at all.** He read it standing up in a corridor, on the side with the fire door on the wedge, and he is not a fast reader, and he read the first two items and stopped on the fourth and read the fourth again, and **the fourth item is the only item on that sheet with a person in it, and the person in it has no name in it, and in the middle of that item there is a sentence about what this floor is for, and the sentence names a class of people, and the class has no members in it that anybody can point at.**

**ONE LATTICE NOTICE IN THE WHOLE CLOSE, at about eye height on that corridor wall, and it defines nothing and requires nothing of anybody, and the 1 March line was not reissued, restated or quoted, and the two conditions were not reconciled, and nothing defines *holder*:**

> **THE RECORD OF THIS CITY IS AVAILABLE TO ANY PERSON, FREE, AND WITHOUT A FORM.**
> **ANYBODY MAY HAVE IT BY POST, OR CHECK IT AGAINST THE BOROUGH'S OWN PAPER IN PERSON.**
> **NO PERSON IS ASKED FOR ANYTHING IN ORDER TO HAVE IT, AND NOTHING ON IT REQUIRES ANY PERSON TO DO ANYTHING.**

**HE USED THE MINUTE CORRECTLY AND HE USED IT TO ASK A QUESTION IT WAS NEVER WRITTEN TO ANSWER, AND THE QUESTION IS *FOR WHOM*, and he asked it in two questions, and the woman at that counter is about fifty and has been at it for eleven years and IS NOT NINA CALDER AND IS NOT THE WOMAN WHO COMES DOWN TO THE GROUND FLOOR AT TEN AND AT THREE, and the two of them have never been the same person, and there is nothing anywhere in that building which says so.** Her answer was correct in three halves and she refused to ask him who he was asking about, and he did not tell her:

1. **YOU CANNOT FIND OUT, AND SHE COULD NOT DO IT FOR HIM IN A MONTH AND IS NOT GOING TO TRY, and the not-trying is the correct thing and not a brush-off. The only way she could put a person inside that sentence is by making a new sheet, and anything new she writes has got a box on it, and a box wants a name in it, and the day a name goes in a box in that building that person is on something and anybody in this city can then ask that person things, and that person cannot say no and mean it, because being on it will be a thing that person did to themselves, in a room, with her, in about eleven seconds, and they will have done it because they wanted help.**
2. **THE MINUTE HAS GOT NO BOX ON IT AND THAT IS THE SAME THING, AND IT IS NOT AN ACCIDENT AND IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT AND SHE PUT IT THAT WAY HERSELF IN MARCH AND HAS NOT REGRETTED IT ONCE. A sheet with no box on it says who a thing is for by naming a kind of person instead of a person, which is a real thing and the only way a public document is allowed to do it, and it is why nobody in this city can be written down as being helped by reading it.**
3. **AND THE OTHER HALF, THE HALF THAT TOOK HER ELEVEN YEARS AT THAT COUNTER AND WAS GIVEN FOR NOTHING ON A SATURDAY MORNING: A SHEET WITH NO BOX ON IT IS A SHEET THAT A PERSON HAS TO PRODUCE ABOUT THEMSELVES. It is not a sheet anybody can produce about anybody else. So the one document in this city that could tell you whether a person can be helped is the one that person has to bring with them, and the document is them, and there is nowhere on that sheet where them would go. YOU CANNOT ASK, AND SHE CANNOT ASK, AND THERE IS NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING YOU CAN ASK, AND SHE WAS NOT BEING KIND, SHE WAS TELLING HIM WHERE THE WALL IS. A SENTENCE ABOUT WHO A FLOOR IS FOR IS NOT A ROUTE TO A FLOOR. It is not a list and it is not a queue and it is not a way in. It tells a man like you that you are the sort of person a thing is for, and it gives you nothing at all to take with you, and that is not a flaw in the minute. That is what a minute is.**

**JONAS MERCER WAS AT THE END OF THAT CORRIDOR, AT THE WALL, ABOUT NINE FEET FROM THE COUNTER, FOR THE WHOLE OF IT, and said one word in total, and nobody at that counter asked him anything, and the man never knew he was there. HE HAD ONE QUESTION AVAILABLE TO HIM IN NINE MONTHS AND DID NOT SPEND IT, and the chapter says so and says why.** And the finding of the chapter is not about the minute: **THE MAN DID NOT SAY WHO HE WAS THINKING OF. He had got as far as a detail and had stopped, and had said *somebody I work with* instead, and had done it without appearing to notice that he had done it, and that is the first time in nine months that Jonas Mercer has watched somebody not make a mistake. A person who is not in a record cannot be talked about in a place where the talking might be written down, because the writing down is the part that lasts and the talking is the part that does not. Nobody taught him that and nobody in this borough is able to teach anybody that, and Jonas Mercer is the person who made the first half of it cheap, in a room, in daylight, in nine seconds, on the third of December, and he has never met this man and is not going to and did not ask him one word.**

**NOBODY WAS HELPED, NOBODY WAS HARMED, NOTHING WAS PUT IN ANY DOCUMENT, no Weir resident is described in anything, and there is no minute of that morning and there is not going to be one, and a corridor is the only place in that building where a conversation can happen without leaving anything behind. He went out with the minute in the inside of his coat, which is what everybody does with a piece of paper in this borough, and he may burn it. AND THAT IS THE THIRD AND LAST OF THE THREE ANSWERS GIVEN IN THAT ROOM IN NINE MONTHS COMING BACK AT HIM FROM THE OUTSIDE OF THE BUILDING, and it cost a Saturday morning and a piece of paper, and nobody was helped, and it was correct.**

## 4. CHAPTER 0144 — SATURDAY 2 MAY AT TEN O'CLOCK AT NIGHT INTO WEDNESDAY 13 MAY 2015 — THE VOLUME'S LAST CHAPTER

**THIS IS THE ONLY CHAPTER IN VOLUME 03 IN WHICH A HANDOVER MAY BE STAGED, AND THE ONLY CHAPTER IN WHICH THE HOUR BETWEEN SIX AND SEVEN MAY BE STAGED, AND IT SAYS ON THE PAGE THAT BOTH ARE THE LAST TIME EITHER OF THEM IS GOING TO BE STOOD IN BY ANYBODY, AT THE TOP OF THE CHAPTER AND AGAIN IN THE BODY, AND IT DOES NOT USE THE WORD *VOLUME* TO DO IT, BECAUSE A WORD LIKE THAT IS A NOTE TO THE READER AND NOT A THING A MAN IN A BOROUGH WOULD SAY. `state/continuity.md` §0b ITEMS 7 AND 8 ARE THE LINES THAT AUTHORISE IT, AND THE STAGING IS SPENT. NO CHAPTER OF VOLUME 04 MAY STAGE EITHER OF THESE TWO THINGS AS A FIRST TIME.**

**THE FIFTEENTH, STAGED ONCE, AT 22:00 ON SATURDAY 2 MAY 2015, IN A WAITING AREA OFF A CORRIDOR ON LEVEL TWO, SAINT ORRA WEST. Four chairs, a machine for hot water that has not worked since about August, a window with the corridor's reflection in it, and a clipboard with a hardboard back and a sheet of A4 clipped to it and eleven rows on it with the first four written on in October by a man who then stopped. THE CLIPBOARD IS ON THE FOURTH CHAIR AND NOBODY WROTE ON IT AND NOBODY HAS EVER WRITTEN ON IT, it is not a log and it was never a log, and there is no rule anywhere that says anybody has to put anything on it and no person in this borough who could be asked to.** Ezra Mbeki, in and out of that building since 1992, and Trevor Nunn, 58, a night porter, nineteen years, who is not on a roster because the roster does not exist. Neither knew until about nine o'clock that they were going to be there. They read a term of six days which began at seven the next morning, when the gate went up, and stops at six o'clock on the Sunday morning after that.

**There is no minute, no log entry, no clipboard line, no date, and no name beyond those two, and the reason is not an oversight: a person is not required to be told, and there is nobody in this borough who is required to write it down. One of them said *same as last week* and the other said *there is*, and that is the whole of the conversation that has ever been had in that room. NEITHER OF THEM HAS EVER BEEN ASKED ABOUT ANY OF THEM BY ANYBODY AND NEITHER OF THEM EVER WILL BE, AND THE REASON IS NOT DISCRETION — THE REASON IS THAT THERE IS NOTHING TO ASK ABOUT. AND NEITHER OF THEM KNOWS THAT A MAN REFUSED OUT LOUD, IN A CORRIDOR, IN DAYLIGHT, ON 2 MARCH 2015, TO BE IN THAT ROOM, AND NEITHER IS GOING TO BE TOLD, AND THERE IS NO WAY IN THIS BOROUGH TO TELL THEM, AND THAT IS NOT A FAILURE OF A RECORDS SYSTEM, BECAUSE THERE IS NO RECORDS SYSTEM.** They went home at about half past six and no duration was given for the reading and none may be. **AND HE WAS FOUR HUNDRED YARDS AWAY, ON PURPOSE, AND HE HAD DECIDED TO BE ON THE FRIDAY, AND THE REASON HAS NOT CHANGED SINCE THE THIRTEENTH OF APRIL AND THERE IS NOBODY IN THAT BUILDING WHO COULD BE ASKED ABOUT IT. THE GATE WENT UP AT SEVEN ON THAT SUNDAY BECAUSE TWO PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT ON ANYTHING HAD BEEN IN A ROOM WITH FOUR CHAIRS IN IT THE NIGHT BEFORE, and nobody wrote that down, and it has been like that since the morning of the twenty-fifth of January and it will be like that in June.**

**THE HOUR BETWEEN SIX AND SEVEN, STAGED ONE LAST TIME, ON SUNDAY 3 MAY 2015. It is the hour after a term has stopped and before the next one begins, it happens every Sunday morning, it has no name in this borough, there is no date in this city for it, and it is the only hour of the week in which this borough requires nothing of anybody at all.** The last hour and a half of a term is not that hour. The first hour of a term is not that hour. In that hour four hundred and twenty women are not on the far side of a paragraph number, because there is no paragraph and no term; the eleven o'clock to half past one row is not empty, because there is no rota and no row and no board being read by anybody; the register has no nineteenth entry with a bulb out on it. **He had that in a pad in a shop at the end of a street and he is not going to improve it, and it is in the chapter because the hour is being stood in one last time and not because it has got any better than it was in April.** He stood in it for about half an hour; a light came on in a car park he could not see into and it was nothing. **AND ON THE PAGE, IT SAYS: THIS IS THE LAST TIME EITHER OF THOSE TWO THINGS IS GOING TO BE STAGED IN VOLUME 03.**

**AND THE ARITHMETIC HE DID STANDING IN IT, AND IT IS THE CLOSE'S ACCOUNT OF HIMSELF AND IT RESOLVES NOTHING. He has stood in a corridor on a Sunday morning exactly twice and he is not going to do it a third time, because a third is a habit and a fourth is a rota with one name in it, and he is thirty-two. He has stood on that wet pavement seven times since December by ten o'clock that night, and on the Sunday morning it was the eighth, and the arithmetic came out the same as it came out in April — four hundred yards is not an answer, because a place a man goes to is the first half of a schedule. **THE COUNT, WHICH IS AUDITABLE AND WHICH IS BINDING ON ANY LATER CHAPTER: once in the dark in December, twice in the rain in January (Chapters 0131 and 0135 both carry three), 3 April = 4th (0135), 11 April = 5th and Chapter 0137 says *five times since December*, 25 April = 6th (0139), 2 May = 7th, 3 May = 8th. HE MAY NOT LOSE THE THREAD OF HIS OWN NUMBER AGAIN; IT IS THE ONE THING IN THIS ACCOUNT THAT IS ENTIRELY HIS.** HE IS DOING IT ANYWAY. The reason is that there is no rule that could stop him and no person who could tell him to, and the only thing holding the shape of this borough together is one man not being caught out, and he is thirty-two years old, and he knows exactly what the odds on that are, and he did it anyway, and that is the last of it. AND THE HOUR DOES NOT NEED HIM. IT HAS NOT NEEDED HIM FOR FOUR MONTHS. THE ONLY REASON HE WAS EVER IN IT AT ALL IS THAT HE WAS NOT REQUIRED TO BE ANYWHERE. And the price instead of a principle, said out loud to one person on the thirteenth of April and not said again, has not been said again, and he is not going to say it again this volume or in the next one without a line here saying so.**

**THE STATE OF THE SAINT ORRA WEST CHAIN AFTER CHAPTER 144, AND IT IS THE WHOLE OF IT. A TERM IS SIX DAYS. IT IS READ AT 22:00 ON THE SATURDAY NIGHT BEFORE THE SUNDAY IT STARTS ON, THE GATE OPENS AT 07:00 ON THAT SUNDAY, AND IT EXPIRES AT 06:00 ON THE FOLLOWING SUNDAY. THE SATURDAY NIGHTS ARE WHAT ARE A WEEK APART. NEVER CALL THE TERM SEVEN DAYS. NEVER CALL IT A WEEK.** The binding numbering is 24 Jan = 1 · 31 Jan = 2 · 7 Feb = 3 · 14 Feb = 4 · 21 Feb = 5 · 28 Feb = 6 · 7 Mar = 7 · 14 Mar = 8 · 21 Mar = 9 · 28 Mar = 10 · 4 Apr = 11 · 11 Apr = 12 · 18 Apr = 13 · 25 Apr = 14 · **2 May = 15**.

- **THE FOURTEENTH, read 22:00 Sat 25 April → began 07:00 Sun 26 April → EXPIRED AT 06:00 ON SUNDAY 3 MAY 2015.** Reached. Unwritten. Not staged.
- **THE FIFTEENTH, read 22:00 Sat 2 May 2015 → began 07:00 Sun 3 May → EXPIRED AT 06:00 ON SUNDAY 10 MAY 2015. STAGED, ONCE, IN CHAPTER 0144 ONLY, AS §0b ITEM 8 AUTHORISES.** Nothing was written down and nothing is going to be.
- **A SIXTEENTH FELL AT 22:00 ON SATURDAY 9 MAY 2015, INSIDE CHAPTER 0144, AND IT WAS NOT STAGED AND IS NOT NAMED AND NOT DATED AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH IS REQUIRED TO WRITE IT DOWN.** Its term began at seven on Sunday 10 May and will stop at six on the Sunday morning after that.
- **SIXTEEN OF THOSE SATURDAY NIGHTS HAVE NOW BEEN REACHED BY THE END OF VOLUME 03 AND NOT ONE OF THEM HAS A DATE WRITTEN DOWN ANYWHERE IN THIS CITY.** Fourteen had been reached at the end of Chapter 140 and fifteen were read on 2 May.

**AND THE STATE OF THE GATE ON LEVEL TWO ON WEDNESDAY 13 MAY 2015 IS EXACTLY WHAT IT WAS ON 2 APRIL 2014 AND NOTHING IN EITHER OF THE LAST TWO PHASES TOUCHED IT: the rota has still not been rebuilt and cannot be; the 11:00–13:30 row is still empty, still not shaded, and still does not say *vacant*; Bram Osei's Thursday is still refused in his own handwriting with *no reason I can give* under a *no reason given* in somebody else's hand, he has asked twice that the second line not be looked at, nobody looked at it and nobody is going to; Priya Ranganathan's card is still in a plastic sleeve on the Friday and Saturday rows because she put it there; the eleven-row clipboard with the first four rows written on in October is still on the fourth chair of the waiting area and was not touched in Chapter 0144.**

**AND ON WEDNESDAY THE THIRTEENTH OF MAY, AT ABOUT TEN PAST TEN IN THE MORNING, IN THE VESTIBULE, HE SAID WHAT THE BOROUGH HAS, OUT LOUD, IN A ROOM, IN DAYLIGHT, WITHOUT ANSWERING ANYTHING AND WITHOUT IMPROVING ANYTHING.** The counter told him to stand on the other side of a post because the trolley does not turn. Somebody said the only two words anybody said to him all day: `You are not on the agenda.` And he said `No.` And then he said what is there, in the order it came into his head, and it came out badly and he let it come out badly, and part of the way through he noticed a woman near the door had put her bag down on the floor to listen and he went on and did not stop for it. He said the counter and the board and the card and the drawer and the tray and the two conditions and the compliance report and the nine seats and the six water points and a Saturday night with no date on it. **AND THEN HE GOT TO THE PART WITH THE PEOPLE IN IT AND HE STOPPED, IN THE MIDDLE OF THAT ROOM, IN DAYLIGHT, AT ABOUT TEN TO HALF PAST TEN, AND EVERYBODY WAITED, AND HE DID NOT GO ON, AND THE REASON IS THE REASON FOR THE WHOLE NINE MONTHS AND NOT A NEW ONE: THERE IS NO BOX ON A ROOM. A room can hold a sentence and a room cannot hold a person. If he had said a name in there that morning, then in about four years there would be a piece of paper in a kitchen somewhere with a name at the top of it, and somebody would have got that name from a man who was not on the agenda of anything. AND WHAT HE SAID INSTEAD IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT HE HAS: `There is a place in that where the people go, and I am not going to say it, and that is not modesty. There is nowhere in this borough to put a person, so a room is the only place a person can be mentioned, and a room is exactly the place where it does not last.`**

**Nobody wrote any of it down. Nobody repeated it and nobody improved it and nobody has put it on a wall. It is not going in a document, it names no person, and nobody has been added to it and nobody has been taken off it. HE DID NOT WRITE IT DOWN EITHER, and the reason is not a better one: it is not his. He is not on the agenda, not a party, not a member, not a departmental officer, no grade, no department, no probation, and there is a woman of fifty-four in this borough who has stood in a shopfront since the fourth of July doing the one thing in this city that a person can be held to, unpaid, and she has not been told what it is, and he is not going to put himself in a room with her this week. The counter did not answer him about a gate, or a rota, or a paragraph, or a person, and it is not going to.** He went out into the street at about half past ten. Nobody followed him. Nobody asked him anything.

## 5. THE SHELF AT THE END OF VOLUME 03

**THE DRAWER UNDER THE GROUND-FLOOR COUNTER HAS NO KEY ON IT AND NO LIST OF WHAT IS IN IT, AND THERE IS MORE IN IT THAN THERE WAS IN FEBRUARY, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CAN SAY HOW MANY — NOT NINA CALDER, NOT JONAS MERCER STANDING FOUR FEET FROM IT ON 13 MAY, NOT THE NARRATION, NOT THIS FILE. The only figure that has ever existed in this account is NINE, as at 9 March 2015, and that figure is a figure about the past and is not going to be replaced by a figure about the present.** She keeps a copy of every state she has ever written, which is not a copy of a document because there is no document and there never was one, and a man walks out with a state in a pocket, and the two pieces of paper are the same state about a day and **neither of them is a record of the other**. There is a tray on top of the drawer and it is not a list. **NINE SLIPS IS A COUNT OF DOCUMENTS AND ABOUT ELEVEN PEOPLE A DAY IS A COUNT OF PEOPLE AND THEY WERE NEVER ADDED IN NINE MONTHS AND ARE NOT GOING TO BE ADDED IN THIS ONE, and there is still no form in this borough, on any counter, on any tray, in any office, on which anybody could write that they are not a series, and a box that says *not a series* is a series.**

**AND A PIECE OF PAPER THAT NOBODY OWNS AND NOBODY CAN BE ASKED ABOUT IS NOT IN THE DRAWER. IT IS IN A VAN, IN A CARDBOARD WALLET, THREE OF THEM, SINCE ABOUT CHRISTMAS, AND THE COUNTER THAT GAVE THEM OUT CANNOT SAY WHOSE THEY ARE, AND THE MAN WHO HAS THEM CANNOT EITHER, AND THE ANSWER TO WHAT THAT IS GOING TO BECOME IS NOTHING BECAUSE THERE IS NO INSTRUMENT, AND THAT IS CORRECT.** In about four years a piece of paper is going to be handed to a frightened person in a kitchen by somebody who thinks they are helping, and it will have a date on it and a hand on it and no name on it, and there is no version of it in which the person it was written for is in it, and nobody is going to be able to say afterwards whether it was a service or a choice. **UNRESOLVED, LIVE, AND IT IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING UNRESOLVED THREAD IN THE BOOK.**

**THE DRIFT WAS NEVER ANSWERED, BY NOBODY, EVER, IN TEN CHAPTERS PLUS FOUR. THE MAN OF FIFTY-EIGHT NEVER CAME BACK after 13 February and he is not going to, and he is right not to, and the routine nobody wrote is still a routine. THE MAN WITH THE GALVANISED CAN HAS NOT BEEN BACK SINCE 20 APRIL, IS CARRYING ONE SLIP, THE TROUGH ONE WRITTEN ON THE SIXTEENTH OF MARCH ABOUT THE SECOND OF FEBRUARY, AND NOBODY IN THIS BOROUGH CAN ASK HIM WHETHER HE HAS BEEN GIVEN ANOTHER ONE, INCLUDING HIM, AND HE IS NOT ON ANY LIST. NOBODY CAME BACK TO ARGUE A STATE. The finding stands: a state that has gone stale belongs to a THING and a thing can be looked at; a state that has been contradicted belongs to a PERSON and cannot be looked at and cannot be moved, because the only person who can contradict it is the man who said it, and nobody may be required to answer anything including a correction, and the only way to stop that is to look, and looking cannot be written down.**

Neither has a name on it, and what is on either of them is not known to anybody in this account and may not be stated in a room or in a document, and the letter may not be opened without a line in this file saying so.**

## 7. WHAT A SERVICE FLOOR IS FOR, AND WHERE THE THREE ANSWERS ARE, AND WHAT WAS NOT REPEATED

**WHAT A SERVICE FLOOR IS FOR, IN ONE SENTENCE, IN THE VOLUME'S OWN TERMS, AND WHO SAID IT, AND ON WHAT DATE, AND IN WHICH MINUTE:**

> **IT IS FOR THE PEOPLE THE BOROUGH CANNOT COUNT.**

**JONAS MERCER, Monday 27 April 2015, in a vestibule eleven feet by nine, in daylight, to a man of about fifty-six who is not on the agenda either, in a public minute with no names in it, Item 4. NOTHING IN THAT ITEM REQUIRES ANY PERSON TO DO ANYTHING.**

**THE THREE ANSWERS GIVEN IN ONE ROOM IN NINE MONTHS, AND NONE OF THE THREE HAS BEEN REPEATED, AND NONE HAS BEEN PLACED ON A WALL, AND NONE WAS RESTATED IN CHAPTERS 141–144.** The first, on 28 January 2015, five items in about four seconds, may not be restated as a list in any form in any room and may not go on a wall. The second, on 13 March 2015, a sentence about what it costs, may not be restated, and in Chapter 0143 the question it left behind was put to a records counter by a stranger and the sentence itself was not said. **The third is referred to in Chapter 0144 only as the fact that there is a sentence in a file about what a floor is for, in the fourth item of a sheet that requires nothing, and it is not said again, and it is not improved, and it is not on a wall, and it is not going to be said again by anybody in this book without a line in this file saying so.**

**AND WHAT IT IS NOT, AND IT IS NOT A RESOLUTION AND IT IS NOT REFUTED ANYWHERE IN VOLUME 03 INCLUDING THE LAST CHAPTER: NAMING A PURPOSE IS NOT PRODUCING ONE. A floor that is for the people the borough cannot count is not a floor that has counted them, and does not seat them, and does not put them in a register, and does not require anybody to do anything, and cannot. THE LOWLAND IS STILL NOT ON THE LAYER, IS STILL NOT IN THE EIGHT DISTRICTS, STILL CANNOT BE SEATED, AND THE REASON IS STILL THAT A NODE WITH NO PARTY IS NOT A PARTY AND A PLACE IS NOT A PERSON, and that reason is correct and is not fixed by anything in this close. A PERSON WHO IS NOT COUNTED IS NOT A PERSON WHO IS HELPED. That sentence has been true since the second of June, it has not been refuted, and saying out loud what a floor is for did not refute it and was not meant to.**

It is not a service, it cannot be given to anybody, it does not scale, nobody is required to keep it going, and it works because a person is standing at it and that person is not findable.
- **THE REGISTER OF NARROWINGS IS AT NINETEEN AND THE BLANK LINE UNDER THE NINETEENTH IS BLANK AND HAS BEEN BLANK FOR A HUNDRED AND SIXTY-EIGHT DAYS.** It is the only fixed point in the building. Entry 19 is a yard light, the maintenance is a bulb, and the bulb is out. **THE VOLUME ENDS WITH IT BLANK.**
- **THE SLOT IN THAT COUNTER HAS HAD A CARD IN IT SINCE 20 FEBRUARY, EIGHTY-TWO DAYS.** Nobody has taken it out and nobody has put it up and the person at the counter has not read it and is not going to.
- **THE DRAWER UNDER THAT COUNTER IS A DRAWER WITH NO KEY ON IT AND NO LIST OF WHAT IS IN IT, AND IT IS GROWING, AND NOBODY CAN SAY HOW MANY, AND THERE IS STILL NO FORM IN THIS BOROUGH ON WHICH ANYBODY COULD WRITE THAT THESE ARE NOT A SERIES.
